questions.q: How consistent is plain (non-recursive) WITH CTE syntax across T-SQL, Oracle, MySQL 8.0+, and PostgreSQL?
options: Remarkably consistent — the WITH name AS (...) shape is nearly identical across all four
Completely different on every platform
Only T-SQL and Oracle support CTEs at all
Only PostgreSQL and MySQL support CTEs at all
questions.explain: A plain CTE's WITH name AS (...) SELECT shape is one of the more portable areas of SQL syntax across these four dialects.

questions.q: Which two platforms REQUIRE the RECURSIVE keyword for a recursive CTE?
options: MySQL (8.0+) and PostgreSQL
T-SQL and Oracle
Oracle and MySQL
All four platforms require it
questions.explain: MySQL 8.0+ and PostgreSQL require WITH RECURSIVE for a self-referencing CTE; T-SQL and Oracle never require (or have) an equivalent keyword.

questions.q: What is the minimum MySQL version that supports CTEs (WITH) at all?
options: MySQL 8.0
MySQL 5.7
MySQL 5.0
MySQL has never supported CTEs
questions.explain: MySQL only gained CTE support in MySQL 8.0; versions 5.7 and earlier do not support WITH at all.

questions.q: What are the two parts of a recursive CTE called?
options: The anchor member and the recursive member, combined with UNION ALL
The parent query and the child query
The base table and the lookup table
The outer query and the inner query
questions.explain: The anchor member supplies the starting rows; the recursive member references the CTE itself and is combined with the anchor via UNION ALL — this shape is identical across all four dialects.

questions.q: What happens if RECURSIVE is omitted from a self-referencing CTE on PostgreSQL?
options: The self-reference to the CTE inside the recursive member fails to parse
The query runs but only returns the anchor member's rows
PostgreSQL automatically infers RECURSIVE is needed and adds it
Nothing changes — RECURSIVE is optional on PostgreSQL
questions.explain: PostgreSQL (like MySQL 8.0+) requires the RECURSIVE keyword before it will allow a CTE to reference itself inside its own definition; without it, the self-reference fails.
